text: As they walked up the garden, the orange cactus fell, and Mr. Beebe’s last vision was of the garden-child clasping it like a lover, his dark head buried in a wealth of blossom. “It is terrible, this havoc among the flowers,” he remarked. “It is always terrible when the promise of months is destroyed in a moment,” enunciated Miss Bartlett. “Perhaps we ought to send Miss Honeychurch down to her mother. Or will she come with us?” “I think we had better leave Lucy to herself, and to her own pursuits.” “They’re angry with Miss Honeychurch because she was late for breakfast,” whispered Minnie, “and Floyd has gone, and Mr. Vyse has gone, and Freddy won’t play with me.
